page.layout: Two coin medallions (engravings) at the top, side by side; below them one column of running text at full width; no marginal notes; no footnotes.

main_text.p: PHOCAS in eius Imperatoris,& Domini fui,locu succe-dit, quę nuper imperio & vita priuarat:nec tamen ipse ab auaricię vicio tęperauit,cūm caufam ei auaricia Mauricij prębuiffet coniurandi in caput illius:quin longę ftudiofius corradędæ pecuniæ incubuit:& omnia ex Perficæ feruitutis inftituto egit. Hic Romanum Pontifice[?] primarium omnium declarauit follicitatus à Bonifacio 3. Cætera adeò focors & ignauus, & frequentibus adulteriis infamis,ut cūm Ro.imperium undiq; barbari vaftarent,ftarętque folùm eius nominis umbra, confpiratum fit in illum ab Heracliona,Heraclio & Prifco,qui captum inertiffimum hominem prius interfecere quàm ferte ei fuppetias eius milites potuerint,omnémq; ftirpem impuriffimi principis fuftulēre. cœpit imperare anno mundi 4567. à Christo nato 605. imperátque annis 8.Egna.lib.2.

HERACLIVS, qui in Phocam coniurarat, à militibus primùm Imperator pronunciatur: populus dein & Senatus ingenti acclamatione probant:accepto itaq; diademate à Sergio Constantinopolitano patriarcha,Perficum bellum parat,legatis antea miffis pro induciis impetrandis. Ludibrio habitus à Perfis,adeò excanduit ut differre non potuerit: refpondebant enim impij hoftes non prius fe Romanis pacem daturos,quàm Christum abnegaffet Imperator.Perfide igitur omni, in ultionem,igni ferróque vaftata, lignũ falutiferæ crucis recepit..Celebris adhuc eft nobis dies feftus,argumentũ victoriæ infignis: Tigris factus eft inter utrosque limes:nouo tandem morbi genere obiit Heraclius,anno imperij 30.Pom.Læ.Egna.li.2. Tunc Mahomethes infanus emerfit.

page.notes: Coin legends in the two medallion engravings, which are not running text: left, "IMP PHOCAS CAES AVG"; right, "IMP HERACLIVS P F AVG". Doubtful: the tilde over the e in "Pontifice" (line 5 of the first paragraph) is hard to see on the scan. Some letters in the Greek-looking heading lines and the stroke over the final vowels are faint; the transcription follows the most likely reading.
